hero_kpi_rationale: EPAM Systems reached $5.46 billion in revenue in 2025 with 15.4% growth, driven by digital engineering services, cloud and AI, consolidated by the strategic acquisitions of NEORIS and First Derivative.
company_description: EPAM Systems, Inc. provides digital platform engineering and software development services worldwide. The company offers engineering services, including requirements analysis and platform selection, customization, cross-platform migration, implementation, and integration; cloud services for creating a roadmap to set and refine IT and business goals while identifying new and emerging opportunities leveraging cloud technologies; data, analytics and artificial intelligence; customer experience; marketing; and cybersecurity. It also offers operation solutions comprising integrated engineering practices and smart automation services. In addition, the company offers software product and platform development services, which comprise product research, customer experience design and prototyping, program management, component design and integration, full lifecycle software testing, product deployment and end-user customization, performance tuning, product support and maintenance, managed services, as well as cross-platform migration and modernizing legacy platforms. The company serves the financial services; consumer goods, retail and travel; software and Hi-tech; business information and me

kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from digital transformation and software engineering services.
kpis.description: Revenue reached $5.46 billion in 2025, up 15.4% with a 9.2% contribution from the acquisitions of NEORIS and First Derivative in Q4 2024.
kpis.signal: Robust growth driven by AI, cloud and acquisitions

kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting the cost of services, excluding depreciation.
kpis.description: Gross margin came in at 28.8% in 2025 (100% minus 71.2% cost of revenue ratio), up 1.9 percentage points from 26.9% in 2024, reflecting improved operational efficiency.

kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by total revenue, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Operating margin declined to 9.5% in 2025 versus 11.5% in 2024, likely due to post-acquisition integration costs and strategic investments in AI and cloud.

kpis.explanation: Spending related to innovation and development of new technology offerings, as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: R&D expenses (including amortization) represented 1.8% of revenue in 2025, up from 1.4% in 2024, supported by EPAM AI/RUN and DIALX Lab initiatives.
kpis.signal: Accelerating investments in AI and proprietary platforms

kpis.explanation: Total number of employees worldwide at period end.
kpis.description: EPAM had approximately 65,000 employees at the end of 2025, up sharply by 15% driven by the acquisitions of NEORIS and First Derivative in Q4 2024.
kpis.signal: Rapid workforce growth supported by strategic acquisitions

kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of EUR 4.9B in the last year

kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of EUR 0.14B in the last year

kpis.description: Cash & equivalents extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Cash & equivalents of EUR 1.3B in the last year

kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from clients in the financial services sector, EPAM's largest vertical.
kpis.description: Financial Services represented 24.1% of total revenue with $1.32 billion in 2025, up 28.6% from $1.02 billion in 2024, remaining the largest vertical.
kpis.signal: Strong growth driven by digital transformation and AI in financial institutions

kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from clients based in North, Central and South America.
kpis.description: The Americas represented 58.7% of total revenue with $3.20 billion in 2025, up 12.9% from $2.84 billion in 2024, supported by acquisitions and existing demand.
kpis.signal: Solid organic growth in the largest geographic region

risks.title: Uncertain accounting estimates
risks.summary: Accounting judgments and estimates, particularly regarding revenue and business combinations, can significantly impact reported results.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is discussed at the introduction of critical accounting policies, with strong language on estimation uncertainty. It directly affects financial statements and is recurring each year. The Capital category is heavily weighted.

risks.title: Variable revenue recognition
risks.summary: Estimating the amount of variable revenue (discounts, incentives) requires assumptions that may alter reported revenues.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned early in risk factors, with language emphasizing uncertainty and possible material impact. Explicit mention of using judgments for discounts, credits and incentives. Recurring risk heightened by contract diversity.

risks.title: Business combinations and asset valuations
risks.summary: The valuation of acquired assets and assumed liabilities in acquisitions relies on uncertain estimates that can durably affect results.
risks.score_rationale: Discussed in detail with strong terms such as 'inherently uncertain' and 'significant impact on future amortization.' A large portion of purchase price goes to intangible assets. Capital category heavily weighted.

risks.title: Deferred consideration valuation
risks.summary: The value of future contingent payments (earn-out) depends on uncertain forecasts and may result in significant accounting variations.
risks.score_rationale: Mention of complex methods (Monte Carlo) and dependence on financial projections. Changes in assumptions lead to direct accounting adjustments. High position in text and language intensity.

risks.title: Customer concentration
risks.summary: A significant portion of revenues comes from a small number of customers, exposing the company to declines if contracts end.
risks.score_rationale: Although concentration is decreasing, the top 10 customers still represent 21.6% of revenues. Explicit mention of fluctuations related to account maturity. Cautious but not alarming language.

risks.title: Evolution of service models
risks.summary: The transformation toward more complex and integrated services requires new skills and may not be adopted as expected by customers.
risks.score_rationale: The shift to integrated solutions (AI, cybersecurity, cloud) is highlighted as a key evolution. This implies adaptation, skills and customer demand risks. Forward-looking language but with moderate intensity.

ai_positioning.summary: EPAM integrates AI into its services and products, notably through strategic acquisitions. The company uses AI to enhance its offerings and potentially its internal operations.
